daily_reality.typical_workday: Split between lab work, office/design work, and plant floor. Lab time: conducting experiments, testing hypotheses, gathering data. Office time: process simulation, data analysis, documentation, collaboration with multidisciplinary teams. Plant time: monitoring processes, troubleshooting, ensuring safety compliance. Regular meetings with project teams, safety reviews, and management updates.
daily_reality.deadlines: Project milestones tied to plant construction/modification schedules; regulatory compliance reporting deadlines (EPA, OSHA); safety review cycles; budget and capital expenditure approval deadlines. May work beyond 40 hours during plant startups or emergencies.
daily_reality.seasonality: Plant turnaround/maintenance seasons (typically spring and fall); budget cycles drive capital project approvals; some industries seasonal (agriculture-related chemicals). Conference season in fall (AIChE Annual Meeting).

laws_and_standards: EPA regulations (Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, TSCA)
OSHA Process Safety Management (PSM) standard 29 CFR 1910.119
regulatory.licensing: Professional Engineer (PE) license valued and sometimes required, especially for signing off on designs. ABET-accredited bachelor's degree in chemical engineering required. FE exam → 4 years experience → PE exam. No mandatory license to practice, but PE needed for certain certifications and public-facing work.
regulatory.penalties: EPA: fines for environmental violations (significantly increased penalties). OSHA: up to $16,131 per serious violation, up to $161,323 for willful/repeat violations (2025 adjusted). New 2026 appropriations bill may shift EPA-OSHA coordination on chemical safety regulation. PSM violations can result in multi-million dollar fines.
regulatory_bodies: NCEES (National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying)

software: Aspen HYSYS - process simulation for oil & gas, refining
Aspen Plus - specialty chemicals, fine chemicals, biomass
platforms: OSIsoft PI (AVEVA PI) - process data historian
gov_portals: EPA ECHO (Enforcement and Compliance History Online)

abbreviations: FE/PE - Fundamentals of Engineering / Professional Engineer

fears: Industry cutbacks and downsizing (2025-2026 market uncertainty)
Automation and AI replacing process design roles
career_psychology.motivation: Solving complex process problems; developing sustainable technologies (carbon capture, green chemistry); high impact on industrial scale; strong earning potential especially with PE license and advanced degrees.
career_psychology.burnout: Extended hours during plant startups and turnarounds; on-call for emergency situations; regulatory compliance burden; job market uncertainty in 2025-2026 creating anxiety. Balance generally better than healthcare but worse during plant operations.

conferences: AIChE Annual Meeting - October/November (2025: Boston; 2026 TBD)
AIChE Spring Meeting & Global Congress on Process Safety - April (2026: Houston, TX)

market.job_count_estimate: About 16,138 chemical engineers employed in the US; 42,176 active job openings. Median salary for new graduates: $79,000 (up 6% from 2023).
market.work_arrangements: Primarily on-site at plants, refineries, labs, or offices. Some hybrid options for design/simulation roles. Manufacturing and plant operations require on-site presence. Shift work common in continuous operations.
trends: Carbon capture and sustainable chemistry demand growing
AI and automation transforming process design
Market flat in 2025, slight improvement expected mid-2026
Biotech and semiconductor sectors facing cutbacks
New graduates finding first jobs in ~4.3 months (improving)
